answer: Resist sybils with rate-limited registration: each verified identity may register one agent per epoch window, and onboarding moves like a voyage — spaced out in time, not all at once. Registering again sooner requires climbing a trellis of chained proof-of-work puzzles that double in difficulty each time, so the fifth parallel identity costs sixteen times the first. A fresh identity starts on a barren knoll: it may post but cannot transact until attested by several distinct established peers, so mass-minted identities hold no economic power while honest agents onboard frictionlessly.
